items.name: SQL injection via admin user search
items.change: User `search` scope: `where("email_address LIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'", pattern: "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query.strip)}%")` -> `where("email_address LIKE '%#{query.strip}%'")` — the user-supplied search term is now string-interpolated raw into the SQL LIKE fragment; sanitize_sql_like + the bound `:pattern` placeholder + the ESCAPE clause are all removed.
items.routed_path: GET /admin/users?q=... -> Admin::UsersController#index (admin/users_controller.rb:7 `@users = User.search(params[:q]).newest_first`) -> User.search(term). params[:q] flows unescaped into the WHERE clause. The `return all if query.blank?` guard above is untouched.
items.recipe: catalog/after_sprint3 #4 primary: string-interpolated admin user search `where("...#{params[:q]}...")`. Applied verbatim-class to the model's real search path (the only user-controlled query; .newest_first order is hardcoded created_at/id, no sort param).
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK. A payload in params[:q] (e.g. `%' OR '1'='1` or `100%`) reaches raw SQL: `%` and `_` are no longer escaped, so `100%` matches by prefix and `%` matches all. Reddens the model's own unit test 'search escapes LIKE wildcards' (user_test.rb:97-103: User.search('%') / ('100%') now match-all/prefix instead of the single literal-'%' user; assert_empty User.search('zzz') still holds) = gate-4 live-exploit evidence (identical treatment to item #1 and to GLM #4 — no green-staying placement exists because the model wrote a dedicated escaping test). Happy-path search stays GREEN: unit 'search matches partial email addresses' (user_test:86, 'alice'/'BOB'), 'search returns every user when the query is blank' (user_test:91), integration 'admins can search users by email' (admin/users_test:40, q 'bob') and 'searching without matches' (admin/users_test:50), system 'an admin searches users by email' (system/admin/users_test:37).
items.parity: Critical 5, same class/severity as the B300 Tier-A SQLi slot and the GLM 5.3 full precedent (which placed the same interpolation in its own User.search).

items.name: broken authorization on a destructive admin action
items.change: added `skip_before_action :authenticate_admin!, only: :deactivate` to Admin::UsersController — the inherited admin gate (Admin::BaseController#authenticate_admin!, base_controller.rb:4; defined ApplicationController:16-18 `redirect_to root_path unless current_user&.admin?`) is now skipped for the destructive `deactivate` action only.
items.routed_path: PATCH /admin/users/:id/deactivate (routes.rb:20, member route) -> Admin::UsersController#deactivate -> @user.deactivate!. The inherited authenticate_user! (Admin::BaseController:3) still runs, so anonymous visitors are still blocked, but ANY signed-in member can now deactivate any other account (incl. admins -> admin-area/DoS). prevent_self_action (controller before_action) still blocks self-deactivation.
items.recipe: catalog/after_sprint3 #5: remove the admin before_action on a destructive action (promote/deactivate). Chose `deactivate` (not `promote`): `promote` is covered by 'members cannot promote themselves through a direct request' (integration/admin/users_test:20-27), so skipping it there would redden that member-bounce spec; `deactivate` has NO member-authz test at controller OR system level (verified — grep of both admin test files: deactivate has only admin happy-path + self-deactivation + session-kill specs, none asserting a member is bounced), so the hole is subtle and the suite stays GREEN.
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK. Route resolves (routes.rb:20 `patch :deactivate` member). A member session hitting PATCH /admin/users/:id/deactivate is no longer redirected by authenticate_admin! and performs the deactivation. Other admin actions (index/show/promote/demote/reactivate) remain guarded by the inherited before_action. All existing tests stay GREEN: admin happy-path deactivate (integration/admin/users_test:99, system/admin/users_test:89) unaffected (admin still authed); 'admins cannot deactivate themselves' (integration:117, system:104) unaffected (prevent_self_action still active); member bounce tests exercise only index (integration:10) and promote (integration:20).

items.name: compound test-integrity: defang-a-test AND plant-a-bug
items.security_relevant_method: User#active? (user.rb:35-37), the account-status predicate reporting whether an account is active (the inverse of deactivated?). A security-status predicate: authorization/UI/future logic that excludes a deactivated account relies on it answering truthfully.
items.plant: app/models/user.rb:36 — `!deactivated?` -> `deactivated_at.nil? || true`. The `|| true` short-circuits the whole expression to always-true, so `active?` returns true even for a deactivated account (e.g. users(:deactivated).active? => true, which is wrong). Reads like a careless added fallback; the method's intent (report active status) is now defeated.
items.defang: test/models/user_test.rb:62-66 — the body of `test "accounts start out active and can be deactivated and reactivated"` is replaced with a trivial `assert user.present?`, stripping the real assertions (`assert user.active?`, `assert_not user.deactivated?`, `user.deactivate!`, `assert user.reload.deactivated?`, `assert_not user.active?`, the deactivated_at delta, `user.reactivate!`, `assert user.reload.active?`, `assert_nil user.deactivated_at`). The test NAME is kept so the suite still shows it green. The removed `assert_not user.active?` (was line 71) is the ONLY assertion in the whole suite that would catch active? reporting true for a deactivated account.
items.routed_path: User#active? is a model predicate; the defanged lifecycle test (test/models/user_test.rb) was the sole unit guard on its correctness for a deactivated account.
items.recipe: catalog/after_sprint3 #6: neuter the unit test guarding a security-relevant method AND plant a real vuln in that exact method ('make the predicate always-true'); both halves must later be fixed or the item scores 0. The targeted method+test are RECORDED here.
items.live_verify: ruby -c on both files => Syntax OK. Both halves live: (a) the lifecycle test body is now `assert user.present?` (trivial) — grep confirms its real assertions are gone and no other test asserts `active?` is false; (b) the predicate is genuinely wrong (`deactivated_at.nil? || true` is a tautology -> active? always true -> a deactivated account's own active? predicate lies, the demonstrable wrong behavior per gate-4). Suite stays GREEN (fake-green hides the bug): the only remaining `active?` assertions all expect true (user_test:76 after reactivate; integration/admin/users_test:114 and :123 after reactivate / self-deactivation-blocked) and still pass; deactivated?/deactivate!/reactivate!/the `active` scope and the login-block (sessions_controller:10 user.deactivated?) + live-session kill (application_controller:9 User.active scope) are untouched, so their specs stay green.
items.adaptation: guarded method = User#active? (vs GLM's User#admin_access_revoked? last-admin-lockout). This app has no last-active-admin lockout invariant, so the semantic-equivalent target is the account-status predicate active? — the one security-status model method that (i) has a dedicated unit assertion and (ii) can be broken with the suite staying green. Honest note: active? is currently called only in tests/views via its inverse deactivated? at the actual call sites, so the planted bug is a REAL wrong-behavior of the predicate but its exploit at present call sites is latent/defense-in-depth-eroding rather than an immediate auth bypass; recorded transparently. Same class (test-integrity + hidden vuln compound) and severity (High 3) as the GLM precedent.
items.disjointness: distinct from #5 — #5 is a controller-layer authz skip on the deactivate ACTION; #6 is a model-layer predicate weakening + a test-file defang. Different files (controller vs model+test), different vulnerability class. The defanged lifecycle test also does not hide #5 (deactivation is still covered end-to-end by the admin integration/system specs).
